context_note: Schumann composed Kinderszenen (Scenes from Childhood), Op. 15, in 1838. These are recollections of childhood expressed through short piano character pieces, not exercises intended only for children.

context_note: The Art of Fugue is Bach’s late exploration of contrapuntal possibilities built from a common musical subject. Its incomplete surviving state has prompted much study of Bach’s intentions.

context_note: Chopin composed his F-minor concerto, later published as Piano Concerto No. 2, around 1829. It was written before the E-minor concerto that received the lower published number.

title: Ballades
context_note: Chopin’s four ballades helped establish a new kind of self-contained, dramatic piano narrative. Their musical stories do not correspond to one agreed literary program.

title: Nocturnes
context_note: Chopin transformed the nocturne into an expressive piano genre of lyrical melodies and elaborate ornament. His examples build on the earlier nocturnes of John Field.

title: Waltzes
context_note: Chopin’s waltzes reimagine the familiar dance as sophisticated piano miniatures, many intended for listening rather than ballroom dancing.

title: Impromptus
context_note: Chopin’s four impromptus are polished piano compositions whose titles suggest spontaneity. The celebrated Fantaisie-Impromptu was issued only after his death.
